title: Barr Resigns Over Fraud Claims
description_medium: Attorney General William Barr publicly stated that the Justice Department had found no evidence of widespread voter fraud that would change the election outcome. His public assessment contradicted Trump's continuing claims that the election had been stolen. Barr announced his resignation on December 14, after the dispute had become a source of sustained tension with the president. A White House official said Barr had resigned voluntarily. The departure removed the department's leader during a period when Trump was pressing officials to validate his allegations and contest his defeat. title: Trump Again Calls for "Termination" of the Constitution
description_short: Trump Again Calls for "Termination" of the Constitution
description_medium: On December 3, 2022, Trump posted on Truth Social that the 2020 election fraud (which courts found nonexistent) "allows for the termination of all rules, regulations, and articles, even those found in the Constitution." This was the clearest statement any major American political figure had ever made calling for the abolition of constitutional governance to restore himself to power. Republican leadership largely stayed silent rather than condemn the statement.
description_long: Trump suggested in a December 3, 2022, Truth Social post that alleged election fraud justified terminating rules and even constitutional provisions. The post followed reporting about Twitter employees' handling of a 2020 New York Post story concerning Hunter Biden's laptop. Trump used those disclosures to renew his false claim that he had won the election and to call for the result to be revisited. The statement escalated his argument beyond challenges pursued within the existing legal framework by invoking the removal of constitutional constraints themselves. Democrats sharply condemned the language. Some Republicans also rejected it, including Mike Lawler and Mike Turner, while other party figures emphasized the approaching nomination process rather than ruling out support for Trump. The response exposed continuing tension over his attempted political comeback and the party's relationship with him. The post was a public demand and provocation, not an enacted change to the Constitution or a legal reopening of the election. Its significance lay in the position he advocated and the reactions it produced.

title: Trump Fires AG Jeff Sessions for Recusing from Russia Investigation
description_short: Trump Fires AG Jeff Sessions for Recusing from Russia Investigation
description_medium: Donald Trump removed Attorney General Jeff Sessions on November 7, 2018, after repeatedly criticizing his recusal from the Russia investigation. Critics viewed the removal as an attempt to gain greater control over an investigation involving the president.
description_long: Donald Trump removed Attorney General Jeff Sessions on November 7, 2018, after repeatedly criticizing his recusal from the Russia investigation. The change came the day after the midterm elections and placed Matthew Whitaker in an acting leadership role. Critics viewed the removal as an attempt to gain greater control over an investigation involving the president. title: Giuliani Hair Dye Runs Down Face at Election Fraud Press Conference
description_short: Giuliani Hair Dye Runs Down Face at Election Fraud Press Conference
description_medium: At a November 19, 2020 press conference at Republican National Committee headquarters in Washington, D.C., where Rudy Giuliani and Sidney Powell presented their sweeping but evidence-free claims of a coordinated international conspiracy to steal the 2020 election involving Dominion Voting Systems, Venezuela, and deceased Cuban dictator Hugo Chavez, Giuliani's hair dye began visibly running down both sides of his face under the hot lights. The rivulets of dark brown liquid streaming past his jaw became a defining image of the post-election period and were broadcast live on major networks.
description_long: At a November 19, 2020 press conference at Republican National Committee headquarters in Washington, D.C., where Rudy Giuliani and Sidney Powell presented their sweeping but evidence-free claims of a coordinated international conspiracy to steal the 2020 election involving Dominion Voting Systems, Venezuela, and deceased Cuban dictator Hugo Chavez, Giuliani's hair dye began visibly running down both sides of his face under the hot lights.
